_comment: Frozen labeled query set for the KB search eval harness (graph task #173 §5/§8, grown per #193). Graded relevance 0-3 (3=primary match, 2=strong, 1=marginal). 44-doc self-contained fixture so `npm run eval` runs offline; pass --gid to score a live graph instead. Designed to SEPARATE tiers, not just be large: (a) vocabulary-overlap clusters (the word 'token' spans docs 2/3/11; 'graph'/'edges' span 8/19) stress lexical precision; (b) paraphrase queries whose relevant doc shares NO query words (e.g. 'stop bots hammering the api' -> doc 3) can only be recovered by the dense leg. Docs 1-12 and q1-q7 are unchanged from the original seed so the set only grows. Every later tier (vector -> BM25 -> rerank -> graph expansion) gets A/B'd against these same numbers.

corpus.title: Cookie-based session storage
corpus.description: Move auth from Authorization header to httpOnly secure cookies
corpus.body: Wrap the session middleware so reads come from Set-Cookie instead of the bearer header. Covers login, refresh, and logout flows.

corpus.title: Audit token usage
corpus.description: Find every call site reading the session token
corpus.body: Grep the auth middleware for header reads. Several API routes call the middleware directly and will need the new cookie-aware helper.

corpus.title: Rate limiting middleware
corpus.description: Throttle abusive clients
corpus.body: Token bucket per IP. Store counters in Postgres. Return 429 with Retry-After when the bucket empties.

corpus.title: pgvector HNSW index
corpus.description: Dense vector search for semantic retrieval
corpus.body: Add an embedding column on tasks and an HNSW index. Tune ef_search per session before rebuilding. Cosine distance over BGE-M3 vectors.

corpus.title: BM25 lexical search
corpus.description: Real BM25 over node content, not vanilla ts_rank
corpus.body: ts_rank lacks IDF and length normalization. Use a proper BM25 extension so the lexical leg has document-length-aware scoring.

corpus.title: Cross-encoder reranker
corpus.description: Rerank the top candidates for precision
corpus.body: bge-reranker-v2-m3 scores query-document pairs. Rerank only the top 20-50 fused hits. The single biggest accuracy lever in the pipeline.

corpus.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
corpus.description: Fuse lexical and dense candidate lists
corpus.body: RRF with k=60 merges the BM25 and vector rankings without score normalization. Rank-based, robust, and parameter-light.

corpus.title: Graph expansion over edges
corpus.description: Multi-hop retrieval across authored edges
corpus.body: Seed from the reranked hits, then traverse the existing edges table k hops, or run Personalized PageRank. We already have the graph, so no LLM extraction.

corpus.title: Kanban view
corpus.description: Group tasks by status into columns
corpus.body: Drag a card between columns to PATCH its status. Edges hidden in this view. Per-user view preference in localStorage.

corpus.title: Presence and selection
corpus.description: Show who is editing what on the live canvas
corpus.body: Each writer posts a selection anchor over SSE. Avatars appear in the top-right bar. Idle presence is reaped after 30 minutes.

corpus.title: Agent tokens
corpus.description: Attribute agent writes to a user
corpus.body: Generate a gt_ prefixed token in the settings panel. The server routes by prefix: gt_ is an agent token, eyJ is a Clerk session JWT.

corpus.title: Optimistic concurrency merge
corpus.description: Three-way merge protects UI-managed fields
corpus.body: PATCH sends base_version and base_content. The server merges so a node's x/y position and color survive an agent rewrite that omits them.

corpus.title: Clerk email OTP sign-in
corpus.description: Passwordless login with emailed one-time codes
corpus.body: Users authenticate by entering a one-time code we email them, so there is no password to store or leak. Clerk issues the code and the resulting session; dev keys stay in dev.

corpus.title: Per-graph roles
corpus.description: Owner, editor, and viewer permissions on each graph
corpus.body: Every membership carries a role. Mutations require editor or owner; viewers receive the live stream read-only and cannot PATCH a node.

corpus.title: Team invitations
corpus.description: Invite collaborators into a workspace
corpus.body: Send an invite to an email address; the recipient clicks a link that adds them to the workspace as an editor. Pending invites expire after a week.

corpus.title: Subscription billing
corpus.description: Paid pro plans through Stripe
corpus.body: Checkout opens a Stripe session. On a successful-payment webhook the account flips to the pro tier and unlocks higher graph limits.

corpus.title: Live event stream
corpus.description: Push node and edge changes to every client
corpus.body: Clients subscribe to an EventSource feed and the server emits a delta for every create, update, and delete. On reconnect the client sends Last-Event-ID to resume without gaps.

corpus.title: Drag to reposition a node
corpus.description: Move nodes around the canvas
corpus.body: A pointer drag updates the coordinates locally for smoothness, then PATCHes the new position on release. Peers receive the move through the event stream.

corpus.title: Author an edge by dragging
corpus.description: Link two nodes together
corpus.body: Drag from a node's connector handle onto another node to create a relationship between them. The edge is saved and becomes available to multi-hop traversal.

corpus.title: In-graph Find bar
corpus.description: Cmd/Ctrl+F filter over the open graph
corpus.body: A keyboard-triggered bar filters the current graph's nodes by substring as you type. It runs entirely in the browser with no server round-trip, the instant client-side lexical leg.

corpus.title: Chunk long bodies for embedding
corpus.description: Overlapping passages for dense retrieval
corpus.body: Long node text is divided into overlapping windows so each vector represents a focused passage rather than a blurred average of the whole document. Unchanged spans are skipped via a content hash.

corpus.title: Write-time embedding indexer
corpus.description: Keep the vector store in sync on save
corpus.body: When a node is written we hash its content and, on a change, re-chunk and re-embed it into the store. Identical content is left untouched so ordinary saves stay cheap.

corpus.title: Modal GPU embedding backend
corpus.description: Serverless T4 serving BGE-M3
corpus.body: A Text-Embeddings-Inference image runs on a Modal T4 behind an HTTP endpoint. It scales to zero between requests and rejects unauthenticated calls at the edge, so idle time bills nothing.

corpus.title: Forward-only migrations
corpus.description: Versioned SQL applied once
corpus.body: Each migration is a numbered SQL file applied a single time and recorded in a migrations table. There are no down migrations; corrections roll forward as new files.

corpus.title: Presence history hypertable
corpus.description: Time-series heartbeats in TimescaleDB
corpus.body: Selection heartbeats are appended to a hypertable partitioned by time. A retention policy drops rows older than the window so the table never grows unbounded.

corpus.title: Health check endpoint
corpus.description: Liveness probe for the gateway
corpus.body: A lightweight route returns 200 only when the database pool answers a trivial query. The supervising gateway polls it to decide whether the worker is alive.

corpus.title: Lazy model load and memory cap
corpus.description: Guard the heap when traffic spikes
corpus.body: The in-process embedding model loads on first use and is shared across requests. Concurrent embeds are bounded so a sudden burst cannot exhaust the available memory.

corpus.title: Inbound webhook receiver
corpus.description: Verified callbacks from external services
corpus.body: POSTs from providers like GitHub and Stripe are checked against an HMAC signature and then routed to a handler chosen by the event type in the header.

corpus.title: Share-link preview metadata
corpus.description: og: and twitter: tags per deployment
corpus.body: Each deployed graph renders Open Graph and Twitter Card tags server-side so a pasted link unfurls with a title, a description, and a thumbnail image.

corpus.title: Weighted rank fusion
corpus.description: Bias the blend of lexical and dense lists
corpus.body: Beyond plain reciprocal-rank fusion, each retriever's contribution can be weighted so a more trusted leg pulls harder on the merged ordering.

corpus.title: Query embedding at search time
corpus.description: Vectorize the user's text per request
corpus.body: At search time the typed text is run through the same model used to index documents, then compared against stored vectors by cosine similarity to find near neighbors.

corpus.title: Ownership filter in search
corpus.description: Never surface another owner's nodes
corpus.body: Cross-graph retrieval applies a WHERE on ownership before ranking and enables strict iterative scan so the access filter does not starve the candidate list.

corpus.title: Progressive search rendering
corpus.description: Paint instant hits, refine asynchronously
corpus.body: The bar shows substring matches immediately, then re-sorts once the slower dense and reranked results arrive, so perceived latency equals the first paint regardless of model time.

corpus.title: Halfvec vector storage
corpus.description: Half-precision embeddings to shrink the index
corpus.body: Storing vectors as 16-bit halfvec halves the index footprint with negligible recall loss at our scale, which keeps the HNSW graph compact and fast to scan.

corpus.title: Reranker licensing note
corpus.description: Commercial-use constraints on cross-encoders
corpus.body: Some popular rerankers ship under non-commercial licenses and cannot be self-hosted inside a product. We default to a permissively licensed model so self-hosters stay in the clear.

corpus.title: Theme color tokens
corpus.description: Light and dark design tokens
corpus.body: Both themes redefine the full set of color custom properties. Components reference semantic aliases, so re-pointing one token reskins a role without editing any component rules.

corpus.title: Markdown frontmatter parsing
corpus.description: Split metadata from the node body
corpus.body: Node content is markdown opening with a fenced frontmatter block. The parser pulls title, description, and the other keys out, leaving the remaining text as the searchable body.

corpus.title: Toast notifications
corpus.description: Transient status messages
corpus.body: Brief confirmations and errors slide in at the corner and auto-dismiss after a few seconds. Stacked toasts queue and the oldest is reaped first.

corpus.title: Keyboard shortcuts panel
corpus.description: Discoverable hotkeys overlay
corpus.body: A help overlay lists every shortcut, including the Find bar trigger, the kanban toggle, and the new-node key. Bindings are customizable per user.

corpus.title: Debounced autosave
corpus.description: Persist edits without a save button
corpus.body: Edits are batched and written after a short idle delay, so rapid typing does not flood the server while every change still persists on its own.

corpus.title: Avatar color assignment
corpus.description: A stable hue per collaborator
corpus.body: Each person is given a consistent color derived from their id, so their selection outline and their avatar in the presence bar always match across sessions.

corpus.title: Deploy to fly.io
corpus.description: Ship the app to a public URL
corpus.body: A deploy builds the container image and releases it to a fly.io app with the project database attached. The assigned public hostname then serves the live canvas.

corpus.title: Agent activity on the canvas
corpus.description: Show automated edits like a person's
corpus.body: Writes from an automation appear with a named avatar and a selection just as a human's do, so the live canvas attributes every change on screen to its author.

corpus.title: Lexical versus semantic retrieval
corpus.description: When keyword search wins and when vectors win
corpus.body: Exact identifiers and rare tokens favor the lexical leg, while paraphrases and conceptual matches favor the dense leg. The hybrid keeps both so neither failure mode dominates a result set.
